title: Maximize the Number of Target Nodes After Connecting Trees I
summary: Given two distinct labeled trees with n and m nodes, represented by their edges, and an integer k, determine the maximum number of nodes in the first tree that can be targets to each node in the first tree by connecting one node from the first tree to any node in the second tree, ensuring each query is independent and the added edge is removed before the next query.
statement: Given two distinct labeled trees with n and m nodes, represented by their edges, and an integer k, determine the maximum number of nodes in the first tree that can be targets to each node in the first tree by connecting one node from the first tree to any node in the second tree, ensuring each query is independent and the added edge is removed before the next query.
constraints: Each edge list describes a separate labeled tree; an empty edge list represents one node; k is nonnegative.
For each first-tree node independently, add one temporary edge between any nodes of the two trees.
A target lies at distance at most k; maximize the target count for each first-tree source.
hints: The temporary edge separates every target path into a first-tree part, one bridge, and a second-tree part.
Count each first-tree radius-k neighborhood; the best second-tree radius-(k-1) neighborhood is a shared bonus.
Run a bounded traversal from every node in both trees, then add the maximum second-tree count to each first-tree count.
Choosing the first endpoint at the queried node never reduces the second-tree reach, so both optimized terms are independent.
editorial: Choosing the first endpoint at the queried node never reduces the second-tree reach, so both optimized terms are independent.

tests.explanation: Choosing the best second-tree endpoint for each query produces counts 9, 7, 9, 8, and 8.
The only first-tree node reaches itself and one chosen second-tree endpoint, totaling two.
